claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition founder) asserts that a founder's high-sacrifice generational sprint lasts approximately 10 years regardless of dream size, so the marginal cost of pursuing a larger dream is zero — the sacrifice is identical whether the goal is small or large. The implication is that goal magnitude is the only free variable, and founders systematically undersize it.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: Founder or entrepreneur choosing a primary multi-year pursuit
claims.mechanism: The cost structure of the 10-year sprint (time, social sacrifice, opportunity cost) is fixed regardless of goal ambition level; since the denominator is constant, maximizing the numerator (dream size) is the rational choice.
bounded_by: Does not address post-10-year capital deployment or scaling phases
Assumes the founder has not yet committed to a specific dream scale

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia argues that founders deliberately suppress disclosure of their largest ambitions — the biggest dream is the one they don't want to tell anyone about — suggesting social fear of judgment is the primary filter that keeps founders systematically under-ambitious.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: Founder in early or pre-commitment phase
claims.mechanism: Social shame and fear of being judged as unrealistic suppress public articulation of ambitious goals; the goals founders self-censor are precisely the correct-scale ones because they elicit the most internal resistance.

practices.text: Make your primary multi-year business goal as large as possible — specifically the largest dream you would be embarrassed to tell others — because the sacrifice required is the same regardless of goal size.
